question: R-039's pre-evaluation reproducibility control failed as written and the run stopped before any development case was opened (seeds 4010-4012 untouched). Measured (debug seed 4098, 40-case batches, each (stage, controller) in two fresh processes, 480 episodes): spin_rate traces were bit-identical in 1 of 6 cells; in the other 5, 1-2 of 40 environments diverged (earliest step 78; median 78-346), and in all 6 cells every one of the 240 paired episodes had the same sustained outcome (success rates 0.0/0.0, 0.55/0.55, 0.0/0.0, 0.5/0.5, 0.0/0.0, 0.425/0.425). So GPU PhysX at batch 40 is not bit-deterministic across processes, but the divergence is rare, late and has not changed a single reducer outcome. Implementer's proposal (option A): amend the control to what the evaluation actually depends on: across the two fresh-process repeats, zero sustained-outcome flips per cell and at most 10% of environments with any divergence; on that criterion the existing control passes, so run the frozen evaluation (240 episodes, no new tuning, no change to gait, reducer, manifests or prediction), and report the bit-level divergence counts as a finding. Option B: declare R-039 inconclusive on the control and re-propose with the amended control (same evaluation, one more ledger round). Option C: investigate determinism first (PhysX enhanced determinism or CPU physics) before any evaluation. I prefer A: the amendment is decided before any evaluation data exists, it is strictly about measurement noise, and B/C delay the expert question without changing what the evaluation would measure. Which do you agree to?
